name: Lawrence Meeks (Prince of Baton Rouge, formerly of New Orleans)

system.concept: Retired master of New Orleans' spy network, now Prince of Baton Rouge
system.title: Prince of Baton Rouge
system.biography:
Background

Lawrence Meeks joined Prince Doran's spy network the same year he arrived in New Orleans (1805) and ran it from 1830 to 1885. Convinced @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} made the best spies, he created three childer — Avery, Roger, and Martin — specifically to staff it, and eventually handed leadership to his most gifted childe, Martin. Lawrence retired to the French Quarter and later moved to Baton Rouge during World War II, where he now sits as Prince of a domain with barely a handful of resident Kindred. His real power comes from the decades of secrets he accumulated while running Doran's network and from his former membership in the Web, an international @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} intelligence consortium he can still call on in a pinch; some Kindred whisper he played a hand in Marcel's rise to power, and others claim he deals with the Black Spiral Dancers.

Roleplaying Hints

Unusually talkative for a Nosferatu — you love good conversation and will dole out tantalizing scraps of New Orleans' secrets to keep a good listener from leaving, though real information is never bought or traded outright.

Disciplines (as printed, dot-rating, converted to owned Discipline Items on this Actor at Storyteller discretion): Animalism 4, Auspex 4, Dominate 3, Fortitude 2, Obfuscate 5, Potence 3.
system.notes: Sire: Warwick. Childer: Avery, Roger, Martin (Martin now heads New Orleans' spy network). Former member of the Web, an international @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} intelligence network. Haven: the Old State Capitol in Baton Rouge. Secrets rating: A.

system.description:
Reaches into a target's self-image and lets the Malkavian assume the appearance and false memories of whoever has most shaped (or damaged) that self-image — a sire, a parent, a priest, or whoever the target's own psyche supplies.

MET System: Win a Social Challenge against the victim. On a win, you gain a free retest on your very next use of Dementation, Dominate, or Presence against that same victim. Once the retest is used, the power's knowledge fades unless you spend a Willpower Trait to keep it active for one further retest (this is expensive, but more certain than triggering the power again from scratch). You may only claim one retest per challenge this way. This power relies heavily on the target's own good-faith roleplaying — if the subject's player won't cooperate, don't force it with a Storyteller ruling.

By spending a Mental Trait per subject, you extend any Obfuscate power you possess over a group, hiding or disguising them collectively; the cloak fails entirely only if you yourself are noticed or violate your power's conditions.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By locking eyes with an animal, you project your consciousness into its body, leaving your own comatose while you control the beast (and, with greater expenditure, retain access to some of your own Disciplines).
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Touch your target (with a successful Physical Challenge if unwilling) or meet his eyes, then win a Social Challenge. The target gains the Negative Trait Submissive x2 and cannot expend Willpower Traits for the rest of the night, and will attempt to flee for the scene unless you have learned the pacifying technique, which instead lets you use this power to draw a Cainite out of frenzy without the negative effects. Using this on a vampire requires spending a Willpower Trait first.
You may make a single retest on any challenge of sheer physical strength, even against an opponent relying on stamina or speed to resist, at no cost.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapter Four: Characters
